skill.name: safe-debug
skill.description: Diagnoses concrete deep learning failures, recommends conservative fixes, and requires approval before patching.
skill.summary: Classify research failures and prepare a minimal, approval-gated debugging plan.
skill.author: lllllllama

content.value_statement: Deep learning failures can invite risky, premature changes. This skill classifies concrete errors and prepares conservative guidance before any code modification.
actual_capabilities: Classifies supplied errors into CUDA, checkpoint, distributed, device, shape, loss, file, runtime, or unknown categories.
Accepts inline error text or reads an error from a UTF-8 text file.
Recommends category-specific checks while withholding patch authorization.
Identifies cases where a savepoint is recommended before patching.
Generates diagnosis, patch plan, and status reports in a selected output directory.
Can emit the analysis to standard output for integration with other tools.
limitations: Classification uses keyword rules and does not inspect repository code.
The skill does not apply patches or verify that a proposed fix works.
The diagnosis report includes only the first twelve lines of supplied error text.
Shared policy references outside the skill directory may be unavailable after installation.

use_cases.title: Triage a Training Failure
use_cases.description: Classify a traceback and identify low-risk checks before changing model code.

use_cases.title: Review a Checkpoint Error
use_cases.description: Separate model variant, checkpoint source, and loading strictness issues before adding compatibility logic.

use_cases.title: Protect Experiment Comparability
use_cases.description: Flag fixes that could change experiment meaning and require an approval-gated patch plan.

prompt_templates.title: Diagnose a CUDA Error
prompt_templates.prompt: Diagnose this CUDA out-of-memory error: {{error}}. Identify the likely cause and suggest configuration-only checks. Do not modify code.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner triage for a memory failure

prompt_templates.title: Analyze a Checkpoint Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this checkpoint loading failure: {{traceback}}. Check model variant, checkpoint source, and strictness assumptions. Propose the smallest fix without patching.

prompt_templates.title: Narrow a Distributed Failure
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this distributed training failure: {{error}}. Use this launch command: {{command}}. Separate environment, configuration, and code hypotheses. Recommend a savepoint if needed.

prompt_templates.title: Audit Research Impact
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit this training failure: {{traceback}}. Consider recent change {{change}} and experiment goal {{goal}}. Explain evidence, uncertainty, reproducibility impact, and a minimal approval-gated plan.
prompt_templates.scenario: Expert review of debugging and research validity

output_examples.input: A training run fails with a CUDA out-of-memory message after increasing image resolution.
output: Check effective batch size, input resolution, and mixed precision before changing model code.

output_examples.input: A checkpoint reports missing keys and size mismatches after changing the model variant.
output: Verify the checkpoint source, selected model variant, and loading strictness.
Create a savepoint before any approved compatibility change.

output_examples.input: Loss becomes NaN shortly after mixed-precision training starts.
output: Inspect data ranges, loss inputs, mixed precision, and learning rate.
Use a short controlled run and require approval before patching.

best_practices: Provide the complete traceback, launch command, and recent relevant change.
Review the diagnosis and approve a specific minimal fix before editing code.
Create a savepoint when the proposed change could affect experiment meaning.
anti_patterns: Do not use this skill for broad repository exploration or refactoring.
Do not treat keyword classification as proof of the root cause.
Do not apply suggested changes without reviewing research comparability.

faq.question: Does this skill change my code?
faq.answer: No. It diagnoses failures and prepares suggestions while keeping patch authorization false.

faq.question: Which failures can it classify?
faq.answer: It recognizes common CUDA, checkpoint, distributed, device, shape, NaN loss, file, and runtime failure signals.

faq.question: Can it inspect my repository?
faq.answer: No. The included script analyzes supplied error text and does not inspect source files.

faq.question: What files does it create?
faq.answer: It can create diagnosis, patch plan, and status reports in the selected output directory.

faq.question: When is a savepoint recommended?
faq.answer: It recommends one for checkpoint, distributed, shape, and NaN loss categories.

faq.question: Can it confirm that a fix works?
faq.answer: No. You must apply any approved fix and verify it with an appropriate controlled run.
